formDescription: Expanded Functional Communication Profile form with concise parenthetical descriptions for question titles and options. Review and customize before use.

items.title: Evaluation Type (reason or timing for completing this profile)
Name (person being evaluated)
Date (date of form completion)
Birthdate (date of birth)
Age (current age at evaluation)
Location (setting where evaluation occurred)
Diagnosis (medical or educational diagnosis information)
Method(s) of Administration (ways information was gathered)
Relationship (for informant interview) (how the informant knows the person)
Speech & Language Evaluation Overview
Level of Impairment (overall severity across major areas)
Relevant History (background affecting communication)

sections.title: Sensory / Motor (sensory, posture, and movement factors)

items.title: Hearing (auditory access and response)
options: May hear yet not react (detection without response)

items.title: Hearing notes (extra details about hearing)
Auditory Localization (ability to notice sound source)
options: Selective to a certain source (responds to only some sounds)

items.title: Vision (visual functioning and access)
options: Impaired (severity or type) (visual difficulty needing details)
Not worn (lenses available but not used)
Lenses not prescribed (no corrective lenses recommended)

items.title: Eye Contact (visual attention to people or objects)
options: Best with objects (better with items than people)
Best with persons (better with people than items)
N/A due to blindness (cannot be judged visually)

items.title: Visual Tracking (ability to visually follow movement)
Visually Inspects Objects (how items are visually examined)
Grasp (hand use and holding ability)
options: Motor impaired, but possible (possible with motor challenge)

items.title: Self-Help Skills (independence in daily tasks)
Head & Trunk Positioning / communication-swallowing implications (posture effects on communication or feeding)
Gross Motor (large body movement abilities)
options: Poor coordination (movement planning or control issues)

items.title: Accepts Being Physically Guided (response to physical prompting)
options: Varies with person or situation (changes across contexts)

items.title: Motor Imitation (ability to copy actions)
options: N/A – lacks vision (cannot judge due to vision)
Gross but not fine motor (large movements easier than small)

items.title: Inappropriate Behavior (behaviors interfering with communication or participation)
options: Stereotyped repetitive motor mannerisms (repetitive body movements)
Stimulus fascination (lights, smells, etc.) (strong attraction to sensory input)
Avoids physical contact or ignores (limited response to physical approach)
Stimulus oversensitivity (high sensitivity to sensory input)
Prefers objects to persons (shows more interest in items)
Poor sensory integration (difficulty organizing sensory input)
Physical aggression (uses body to harm or threaten)
Verbal aggression (uses hurtful or threatening language)
Mouthing inedible objects/body parts (puts unsafe items in mouth)
Poor social boundaries (limited awareness of interpersonal space)
Adheres to nonfunctional routines (rigid routines without purpose)
Preoccupation with object part (focuses on parts rather than whole)
Compulsive or rigid (high need for sameness/control)
Lacks real fear (unsafe underresponse to danger)
Irrational fears (fear response not matching situation)

items.title: Other inappropriate behavior (behavior not listed above)
Attention Span (ability to stay focused)
options: Varies with mood (attention changes with emotional state)
Object preoccupation (focus is captured by preferred items)

items.title: Distractible (how easily attention shifts away)
options: Constantly (attention shifts most of the time)
Depends on task or time (changes with context)

items.title: Alertness (level of wakefulness and readiness)
Response Rate (speed and consistency of responding)
Response Rate - mixed details (notes on receptive versus expressive differences)
Awareness of Others (attention to nearby people)
options: Disregards others (shows limited interest in people)

items.title: Awareness of Environmental Events (attention to surrounding activity)
options: Physical status restricts (physical condition affects awareness)

items.title: Cooperation (willingness to participate)

sections.title: Receptive Language (understanding of spoken, signed, and symbolic input)

items.title: Native Language (first language learned)
Languages Understood (languages the person comprehends)
Oral Comprehension (understanding of spoken language)
options: Direct & indirect requests (understands explicit and implied directions)
Only direct requests (needs very clear requests)
Literal but not figurative (understands exact more than abstract meaning)
N/A due to hearing loss (cannot judge because access is reduced)
Uses sign language (understanding supported by sign)

items.title: Understands Basic Concepts (grasp of common early concepts)
Concepts Understood (specific concepts currently understood)
options: Object function (knows what things are for)

items.title: Responds to Name (reaction when name is called)
options: Sensory loss (response may be limited by access)
With physical prompt (responds with touch cue)
May tune out others (sometimes ignores the call)

items.title: Responds to Attention Commands (No, Stop, Look) (response to basic attention-directing commands)
options: On request (responds to direct verbal cue)

items.title: Looks at Pictures (interest in and attention to pictures)
options: Only with photos (photos work better than drawings)
Items, not scenes (focuses on objects more than whole scenes)

items.title: Accepts Objects Presented (response when an item is given)
options: With gesture (takes item with gesture cue)
With physical prompt (takes item with hands-on support)
Motorically unable (cannot due to motor limits)

items.title: Gives Objects to Speaker (ability to hand items to another person)
options: With gesture (gives item with gesture cue)
With physical prompt (gives item with hands-on support)
Motorically unable (cannot because of movement limits)
Only if exchanging (gives item when it serves a purpose)

items.title: Routine Commands - observed response code(s) (how support was needed for routine commands)
options: V = verbal comments (responded with verbal cueing)
S = signing instruction (responded with sign support)
M = motor impairments (motor issues affected response)

items.title: Routine Commands - types of commands (kinds of routine motor or oral commands followed)

columns: V = verbal comments (responded with verbal cueing)
S = signing instruction (responded with sign support)
M = motor impairments (motor issues affected response)

rows.title: Shake item/limb (shakes object or body part)
Open/close mouth (changes oral posture on cue)

items.title: Environmental Commands (response to directions in daily contexts)
options: Multi-step commands (can follow more than one step)
With written instruction (responds to printed cue)
May understand but is motorically restricted (comprehension may exceed motor output)
Needs situational cues (depends on context to respond)
Follows routine (does best within familiar routines)
Refuses or uncooperative (does not participate willingly)

items.title: Nonverbal Comprehension (understanding of nonspoken communication cues)
options: Other's feelings & thoughts (understands internal states of others)
Body language (reads posture and movement cues)
Voice affect of speaker (reads feeling from voice tone)
N/A due to sensory loss (cannot judge because access is limited)

items.title: Object Identification (ability to identify named or requested items)
options: By function (identifies item by what it does)
With tactile exploration (uses touch to identify)
With limited items (does best with few choices)

items.title: Two-Dimensional Recognition (understanding of photos, symbols, or pictures)
options: Safety signs (recognizes warning or safety symbols)
Requires large pictures (needs bigger visual supports)
Relies on context cues (needs surrounding cues)
Understands picture represents message or concept (grasps symbolic representation)

items.title: Two-Dimensional Recognition - mode of presentation (how picture understanding is shown)
options: On verbal request (responds to spoken cue)
Match object with picture (pairs object to image)
Match picture with picture (pairs picture to picture)

sections.title: Expressive Language (ways the person communicates messages and ideas)

items.title: Languages Expressed (languages used to communicate)
Verbal Status (general expressive communication type)
options: Nonverbal communicator (does not rely on speech)
Total communication communicator (uses many modes together)
Limited verbal communicator (uses some speech inconsistently)
Limited non-oral communicator (uses some nonspoken methods inconsistently)
Lacks communication (functional expression is very limited)

items.title: Expressive Level (check highest level) (highest observed expressive language level)
Methods of Communication (ways the person sends messages)
options: Spelling (letters are used to form messages)
Facial expressions (meaning shown through face movement)
Eye gaze/signal (messages shown through eye direction)
Gestures (body or hand movement conveys meaning)
Word cards (printed word supports are used)
Manipulates others (moves others to communicate wants)

items.title: Self-Expression (topics or purposes expressed)
Quality of Self-Expression (how clear and specific expression is)
options: Must be inferred (listener must guess intended meaning)

items.title: Quality of Self-Expression - variable details (notes on inconsistency)
Object Interaction (how the person engages with materials)
options: Purposeful gaze (looks at items with intent)
Non-purposeful gaze (looks without clear communicative purpose)
Operates for cause & effect (acts to get a result)
Random for self-stimulation (interaction appears self-directed sensory)
Uses adaptive switch (accesses through switch support)

items.title: Most Common Prompting (support usually needed to respond)
options: No response (does not respond to prompting)

items.title: Appropriate Object Use (functional use of objects and materials)
options: With motor limitations (use is affected by movement limits)
With limited items or during ADL (functional only in certain contexts)
Prefers inappropriate items (drawn to nonfunctional objects)
Insists on sameness (prefers fixed use patterns)
Lacks interest or rejects (little interest in items)
Shares or shows others (uses objects socially)

items.title: Operates Cause & Effect Item (ability to activate items for a result)
options: With verbal request (does so with spoken cue)
Physically unable (cannot due to motor limits)
Repetitive in nature (repeats without flexible purpose)
Limited items only (works with only some items)
With adaptive equipment (uses adapted access method)

items.title: Descriptive Language (how scenes, actions, or stories are described)
options: Targets insignificant facts (focuses on less relevant details)
Contains delayed echolalia (uses echoed language from earlier)
Integrated actions (combines more than one action)
Projects self into scene (inserts self into the narrative)
Purely literal (does not infer beyond what is seen)
Narrates with dialogue (includes spoken character lines)
Supplements verbal with gestures (uses gesture to add meaning)
Defines central theme (the "big picture") (grasps main idea)
Deduces conclusion (infers what follows or means)
Comments on thoughts or feelings (describes internal states)
Misinterprets or distorts theme (does not accurately derive main idea)
N/A – visually impaired (visual description is not applicable)

sections.title: Basic Communication Expression (forms used to express basic communication functions)

items.title: Basic Communication Expression Matrix (methods used for basic expression types)

rows.title: Alphabet set (uses letters to build messages)
Picture system / PECS (uses pictures to communicate)
Shows ID tag or card (uses identification support)
Head nod answer (answers by head movement)

items.title: Uses Common Gestures (use of everyday gestures)
Grammar Skills (quality of grammar in communication)
Grammar Skills - means (notes explaining grammar rating)
Vocabulary (overall breadth of word knowledge)
Vocabulary Types Used (types of vocabulary currently used)
options: Physical & emotional states (feelings or body-state words)

items.title: Average Phrase Length (words) (typical number of words per utterance)
Imitation Span (words) (longest verbal imitation length)
Indicate Means (mode used for phrase length or imitation)
Other means details (description of another communication mode)

sections.title: Pragmatic / Social Language (social use of communication across people and contexts)

items.title: Communicative Intent (reasons the person communicates)
options: Describe item/act (describes what is seen or done)
Inform about others (shares information about someone else)
Show interest in others/activity (engages socially around others)
Share interests/objects with others (shares attention or items)
To play with others (communicates for play)

items.title: Other communicative intent details (additional communication purposes)
Initiates Communication (how often communication starts independently)
options: Only egocentric (initiates mainly around own wants)

items.title: Answers Who, What, & Where Questions (ability to answer simple wh-questions)
Answers When, Why, & How Questions (ability to answer more complex wh-questions)
Answers Yes/No Questions (accuracy of yes/no responding)
options: Only concerning needs or desires (accurate mainly for preferred topics)

items.title: Asks Questions (ways the person seeks information)
options: Uses changes in vocal inflection (signals a question by tone)
Reported but not observed (described by others only)
Only concerning self (asks mainly about own needs)

items.title: Conversational Skills (overall back-and-forth interaction ability)
options: Vary with mood (changes by emotional state)

items.title: Communication Partners (people the individual communicates with)
options: Peers or coworkers (same-age peers or colleagues)
Poor interest in relationships (limited social motivation)

items.title: Other communication partners (additional partner types)
Conversational Topics (types of topics discussed)
options: Of mutual interest (shared topic with others)
Appropriately about self (self-related but socially expected)
About rituals (focuses on routines or sameness)

items.title: Turn-Taking (ability to share conversational turns)
options: Fails to attend to listeners (does not orient to partner)
Dominates the conversation (takes too many turns)

items.title: Topic Initiation (ability to start topics)
options: Only with assistance or prompting (requires support to start)
N/A – no means (cannot initiate due to access limits)
Excessive for odd (circumscribed)/unusual topics (initiates restricted topics often)

items.title: Topic Maintenance (ability to stay on a topic)
options: Prompted (needs support to stay on topic)

items.title: Topic Elaboration - number of different statements (amount of detail added to a topic)
Topic Elaboration (supports needed to expand a topic)
options: Indirect verbal cues (benefits from subtle spoken support)
Direct verbal prompts (needs clear spoken cue)
With graphic cues (benefits from visual support)
Only for fixations (elaborates mostly on restricted interests)
Not stimulable (does not improve with cueing)

items.title: Cause-Effect Reasoning (understanding of why things happen)
options: Appropriate response or explanation (shows accurate causal understanding)
Routine/rote response or explanation (relies on memorized response)
Fair response or explanation (partial understanding present)
Only if prompted or directed (needs support to explain)

items.title: Shares Personal Data (ability to share personal information)
Appropriateness of Communication (fit between communication and context)
Considers listener’s perspective? (awareness of another person’s point of view)
options: No (does not yet show perspective taking)

items.title: Uses social rules? (use of expected social communication rules)
Descriptive Conditions (features that describe appropriateness)
options: Knows where to say it (matches message to place/context)
Knows what to say (selects suitable content)
Knows when to say it (times messages appropriately)
Impaired topics (topic choices are limited or unsuitable)

items.title: Discusses News Events (ability to talk about events or information)
options: Unaware/no interest (does not know or care about events)
Rote repetition without meaning or relevance (repeats without understanding)
Unable to express (cannot communicate about events)

items.title: Reading / Literacy (current reading-related skills)
options: Survival words (reads safety or daily-use words)

items.title: Writing / Spelling (current writing-related skills)
Memory - Short Term (recent recall and short-term memory)
options: No recall (does not retain recent information)
Not testable (could not be meaningfully assessed)

items.title: Memory - Long Term (long-term recall and stored knowledge)
options: No recall (does not show retained past information)
Not testable (could not be meaningfully assessed)
Savant-like skills or calculations (shows isolated advanced memory/calculation skills)

items.title: Intelligibility (how understandable speech is to listeners)
options: Easily understood by others (speech is generally clear)
Understood with minor difficulty (small effort is needed by listener)
Understood with moderate difficulty (context helps significantly)
Understood with major difficulty (speech is hard to interpret)
Nonverbal or N/A (speech does not apply)

items.title: Proficiency Level (largest speech unit used clearly)
options: Context must be known (listener needs background to understand)

items.title: Understood By (who can understand the person’s speech)
options: Familiar others (people who know the speaker)
No one (speech is not understood functionally)
Dialect may interfere with intelligibility (accent/dialect affects perception)

items.title: Adjusts Speech to Improve Understanding (ability to repair or clarify speech)
options: No change required (speech already clear enough)
Requires constant cues (needs frequent support to repair)

items.title: Sounds Produced (speech sound inventory currently present)
options: Beginning (vowels, p, b, m, h, w, n, ng) (early-developing sounds present)
Intermediate sounds (y, k, g, f, d) (mid-level sounds present)
Advanced intermediate (t, ch, r, sh, s, v, l) (later-developing sounds present)
Advanced (th, j, zh, z, wh) (more advanced sounds present)
Non-speech sounds (only nonword vocal sounds are produced)
Age appropriate (sound inventory fits age expectations)
Delayed (sound development is behind expected age)

items.title: Error Phonemes (speech sounds produced incorrectly)
Omitted Phonemes (speech sounds left out)
Dentition (teeth and oral structure status)
options: Open bite (teeth do not close fully)
Some teeth are missing (partial dentition present)

items.title: Articulators (status of lips, tongue, jaw, and related structures)
Oral-Motor Imitation (ability to imitate oral movements)

sections.title: Voice (vocal loudness, quality, and pitch features)

items.title: Loudness (voice volume characteristics)
options: Inadequate (volume is too soft or weak)
Inappropriate to setting (volume does not fit context)
Reduced breath support (airflow limits vocal strength)

items.title: Vocal Quality (sound quality of the voice)
options: Cul-de-sac resonance (sound trapped in vocal tract)

items.title: Pitch (perceived highness or lowness of voice)
options: Lower range (pitch is lower than expected)
Immature for age (pitch pattern seems younger)
Mimics other's pitch (copies another speaker’s pitch)
Inappropriate rising inflection (excess upward pitch endings)
Changes for ritual speech or echolalia (pitch linked to scripted output)
Inappropriate for gender (pitch differs from expectation for gender presentation)

sections.title: Oral (oral mechanism, saliva control, and swallowing factors)

items.title: Mouth Breather (how often breathing occurs through the mouth)
options: Most of the time (mouth breathing is common)
Some of the time (mouth breathing occurs intermittently)
Due to nasal congestion (mouth breathing linked to blockage)

items.title: Drooling (presence and management of saliva loss)
options: Nearly always (present most of the time)
Medication prescribed (medical support is in place)
Requires protective measures (needs bibs or other protection)

items.title: Tongue Thrust (forward tongue movement pattern)
Swallowing & Diet (feeding, swallowing, and diet texture needs)
options: Aspiration risk (risk of material entering airway)
Coughing observed (signs of airway concern noted)
Spillage (food or liquid loss from mouth)
Rapid eating/stuffing (intake pace is unsafe or fast)
Food pocketing (retains food in cheeks or mouth)
Uses adaptive equipment (needs special feeding tools)
Modified health diet (follows medical diet plan)

items.title: Adaptive strategies (supports for safer or more effective eating)
Fluency (speech smoothness and disfluency patterns)
options: Adequate (speech flow is within expected range)

items.title: Secondary mannerisms (associated movements during speech)
Rate of Speech (speed of spoken output)
options: Differs for echolalia (rate changes during echoed speech)
Increases for ritual speech (faster with scripted output)

items.title: Rhythm & Intonation (speech melody and prosody patterns)
Changes stress re: meaning? (ability to shift emphasis for meaning)
Other rhythm & intonation description (additional prosody notes)

sections.title: Non-Oral Communication (communication through signs, symbols, or AAC)

items.title: N/A (verbal)? (whether this section does not apply because speech is primary)
Use of Sign Language (current sign language use)
options: Not stimulable (does not demonstrate even with help)
With motor limits (use affected by movement difficulty)

items.title: Meaning of Signs (whether signs are understood or expressed)
Level of Signs (complexity of sign use)
Sample Signs (examples of signs used)
Two-Dimensional Expression (use of pictures or symbols to express messages)
options: Sequence of icons (combines more than one symbol)

items.title: Express Yes/No (methods used to communicate yes or no)
options: Accepts vs. rejects item/activity (shows choice through behavior)
Spells with alphabet board (uses letters to respond)
None or random (no reliable yes/no method)

items.title: Current System & Effectiveness (present communication system and how well it works)
Fine-Motor Abilities (hand skill level affecting access)
options: No limitations (fine motor access is functional)
Non-functional (fine motor access is not usable)

items.title: Recommended Communication System & Potential (best-fit AAC or communication supports)
Test Results (formal or informal assessment findings)
Current Communication Objectives (present communication goals)
Communication Strengths (areas of relative strength)
Communication Weaknesses / Needs (areas needing support)
General Intervention Strategies (broad treatment recommendations)
Related Plans in Other Settings (supports used across environments)
How Residential & Day Program Plans Coordinate (coordination across care settings)
How to Integrate Communication with Other Disciplines (Psych., P.T., O.T., Rec.) (team-based collaboration recommendations)
Recommendations, Progress, Referrals & Medical Necessity (clinical recommendations and justification)
Speech-Language Pathologist (clinician completing the report)
Evaluator (person conducting the evaluation)
Phone (contact number)
Email Address (mailing or email address)
